title: Tim Smedley
gist: An author index page (not an article) for environmental writer Tim Smedley, editor of the New Climate and author of The Last Drop on the world water crisis; the 22 listed headlines map Prospect's climate coverage agenda — a hardening case against data centres, scepticism of heat pumps, a 2025 solar boom, solar geoengineering, and opposition to new drilling.

themes.theme: Prospect's climate and energy editorial agenda

insights.claim: Prospect is running an environmental argument that the case against data centres is growing, positioning datacentre buildout as a contested land, water and energy issue in UK public debate rather than a purely technological one.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Rising UK media hostility to data centres is a permitting and social-licence risk for AI infrastructure siting — watch for planning friction.
insights.quote: The case against data centres is growing
insights.locator: Environment / The case against data centres is growing

insights.claim: The same environmental writer argues both that 2025 was a great solar boom and that heat pumps are the wrong answer for heating homes, implying a pro-renewables but heat-pump-sceptical position on UK decarbonisation policy.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Elite-media scepticism about heat pumps undercuts the UK's flagship heating-decarbonisation subsidy, while solar sentiment stays strongly positive.
insights.quote: Forget heat pumps—this is how to heat our homes

insights.claim: Prospect's climate coverage explicitly opposes more drilling and frames current policy as complacency, indicating continued UK media pressure against new hydrocarbon licensing.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Political cost of new UK drilling approvals stays elevated regardless of energy-security arguments.
insights.quote: This is no time for climate complacency—let alone more drilling
insights.locator: Climate / This is no time for climate complacency

insights.claim: Solar geoengineering has moved into mainstream UK ideas journalism, with coverage framing scientists' plans to block out the sun as a question of how worried the public should be.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Geoengineering entering popular discourse is an early marker of climate-adaptation and intervention spending becoming politically discussable.
insights.quote: Scientists want to block out the sun. How worried should we be?
insights.locator: Climate Change / Scientists want to block out the sun

insights.claim: The writer's book The Last Drop: Solving the World's Water Crisis and his editorship of the New Climate signal water scarcity as a distinct, book-length investible theme separate from carbon.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Water-crisis framing is gaining dedicated authorial and editorial infrastructure — a slow-building theme for water infrastructure and utilities exposure.
insights.locator: Tim Smedley is an environmental writer
